# hyperfluid_rabbitmq (Resource)

A managed RabbitMQ broker. The platform generates its credentials and stores them in the secret manager; this resource only reports where they are (the `*_secret_name` attributes), never their values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "hyperfluid_env" "default" {
  name = "default"
}

resource "hyperfluid_rabbitmq" "orders" {
  env      = data.hyperfluid_env.default.id
  name     = "orders"
  replicas = 3      # 1, 3 or 5; can only grow
  storage  = "20Gi" # per node; can only grow
  plugins  = ["stream", "shovel"]

  resources = {
    requests = {
      cpu    = "500m"
      memory = "1Gi"
    }
    limits = {
      memory = "2Gi"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials live in the secret manager; the provider only exposes their
# names. Reference them from an app with `secret:<name>`.
output "amqp_uri_secret" {
  value = hyperfluid_rabbitmq.orders.amqp_uri_secret_name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `env` (String) Environment id the broker runs in. Changing this forces a new broker.
- `name` (String) Broker name (RFC 1035 label, at most 59 characters). Changing this forces a new broker.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form description.
- `image` (String) RabbitMQ container image. Omitted, the broker tracks the platform-pinned image, resolved at reconcile time, and this stays null; removing it after it was set keeps the current pin.
- `plugins` (Set of String) Optional plugins to enable, from the allowlist: `stream`, `shovel`, `federation`, `mqtt`. The management, Prometheus and Kubernetes peer-discovery plugins are always on. Defaults to none.
- `replicas` (Number) Number of broker nodes: `1`, `3` or `5`. Can only grow: a RabbitMQ cluster cannot be scaled down, so a lower value is rejected at plan time. Omitted, the platform default applies and is never written into state; removing it after it was set keeps the current node count.
- `resources` (Attributes) CPU and memory requests and limits per node. Omitted, the platform default applies. Leaving `limits.cpu` unset avoids CPU throttling. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resources))
- `storage` (String) Volume size per node, a whole Kubernetes quantity such as `"20Gi"`. Can only grow: a smaller value is rejected at plan time. Omitted, the platform default applies and is never written into state; removing it after it was set keeps the current size.
- `tags` (List of String) User-defined tags.

### Read-Only

- `amqp_port` (Number) AMQP port, once provisioned.
- `amqp_uri_secret_name` (String) Secret-manager name of the AMQP connection URI, credentials included (reference it with `secret:<name>`).
- `host` (String) Broker host, once provisioned.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `management_port` (Number) Management (HTTP API) port, once provisioned.
- `management_uri_secret_name` (String) Secret-manager name of the management API URI, credentials included (reference it with `secret:<name>`).
- `password_secret_name` (String) Secret-manager name of the broker password (reference it with `secret:<name>`).
- `phase` (String) Current lifecycle phase.
- `slug` (String) Derived slug.
- `username_secret_name` (String) Secret-manager name of the broker username (reference it with `secret:<name>`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# RabbitMQ broker import id is the broker id (uuid).
terraform import hyperfluid_rabbitmq.orders 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
